thread:
liz: Quick ask — after the runtime change yesterday I'm seeing ~12% p50 latency regression on our on-prem KVM VMs vs the baremetal lab. Can someone help repro / sanity-check env parity? Details below.

omar: Which model + harness + seq len? paste the exact bench command you used.

liz: Model: llama-13b-quant (kv cache on), seq=1024, batch=1. Harness: `bench/run_inference.sh --model llama-13b-quant --seq 1024 --batch 1 --warm 20 --iters 200`

liz: Host is KVM on metal (libvirt/qemu), qemu 7.3, virtio-net + virtio-scsi. Hugepages: using 1G pages, reserved 2G. Kernel: 6.6.x.

ken: Do we see the regression only on VMs or also on Dedicated hosts? Also, can you include perf stat output?

liz: Only on the VMs we manage in DC-A. perf stat snippet from the run attached:
```
$ sudo perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-references,cache-misses,context-switches -a -r 3 bench/out/perf_run
Performance counter stats for 'bench/out/perf_run':

        2,130,412,345 cycles
        1,049,234,567 instructions
          25,432,120 cache-references
           1,123,456 cache-misses
         201,234 context-switches
```

liz: The context-switches number feels high compared to baremetal (~28k). Not sure if it's the virt drivers or CPU isolation.

nidhi: Can you check cpufreq and C-states? Also whether irqbalance is running and how interrupts are pinned. On KVM we often forget `isolcpus`/`nohz_full` for the worker vCPU.

liz: quick checks: `cat /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor` -> returns 'ondemand' on the host. irqbalance is active. I didn't set isolcpus.

omar: Try these quick experiments (one at a time):
- set host governor to 'performance'
- stop irqbalance and manually pin IRQs to management CPU
- boot guest with `-cpu host -realtime mlock=on` and add `isolcpus=... nohz_full=...` on kernel cmdline for the pinned vCPUs

omar: Also can you toggle IOMMU? i've seen virtio/vhost behaviour differ with `intel_iommu=on|off`.

liz: running a short diagnostic now. perf record command I'm using: `sudo perf record -F 200 -a -g -- bench/out/perf_run` — will upload perf.data to s3 when done.

ci-bot: Benchmark job #482 finished. Summary: p50=123ms (+12%), p95=312ms (+9%). Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/bench/482/{perf.data,flamegraph.svg}

ken: If you can, share the qemu cmdline (libvirt XML) — common culprits: missing `-mem-prealloc -mem-path /dev/hugepages`, vfio options, or enabling vhost_net vs slirp.

liz: snippet from /etc/libvirt/qemu/llama-vm.xml (sanitized):
```xml
<domain type='kvm'>
  <name>llama-vm</name>
  <memory unit='GiB'>64</memory>
  <currentMemory unit='GiB'>64</currentMemory>
  <vcpu placement='static'>8</vcpu>
  <cpu mode='host-passthrough'/>
  <memoryBacking>
    <hugepages>
      <page size='1073741824' unit='bytes' />
    </hugepages>
  </memoryBacking>
  <devices>
    <interface type='network'>
      <model type='virtio'/>
    </interface>
  </devices>
</domain>
```

nidhi: Looks okay on paper. Two things to try: ensure guest is using hugepages (check /proc/meminfo inside guest) and compare `/proc/interrupts` and `cat /proc/softirqs`. Also check vhost_net version (`modinfo vhost_net`).

liz: I checked guest /proc/meminfo: HugePages_Total = 0. So libvirt memoryBacking isn't translating to guest hugepages. Hmm.

ken: That's the kicker — if guest isn't actually using hugepages you'll lose predictability (page faults, ballooning). Try `--mem-prealloc` + host hugepage mount and confirm guest is launched with `memfd` backing.

ops-bot: Reminder: perf.attach logs uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/bench/482/perf.data (expires in 7d) :white_check_mark:

omar: Another angle: check kernel scheduler tune: are you on a patched scheduler in the host kernel? sometimes low-latency patches or disabling CFS groups affects throughput.

liz: Thanks — I'll run three configs tomorrow: (1) enable host performance governor + stop irqbalance, (2) ensure guest gets hugepages with mem-prealloc, (3) toggle intel_iommu. I'll share perf.data + flamegraphs and tag you all. cc @nidhi @ken :eyes:

ken: Sounds good. If you want, I can carve out 30m this PM to look at the XML and help repro.

liz: Appreciate it — will ping when uploads are ready. :thumbsup:
